correctness.rationale: Rebuilt the cube's 12 edge-vertices and 24 cuboctahedral adjacencies from bit arithmetic, tested all 792 five-subsets for connectedness (516 disconnected), generated 2,973 nonempty faces with f-vector (12,66,220,495,792,872,516). Independently implemented staged toggling on all faces: 1,418 matched pairs; critical cells in dimensions 0:1,5:15,6:121; verified all 15,576 oriented Hasse covers acyclic. Exact integral gradient boundary is a 15-by-121 matrix of rank 3 with determinant +1 on rows and columns (0,1,6). Thus 12 free degree-five and 118 free degree-six generators, no torsion; the 5-skeleton wedge and degree classification of pi_5 permit unit cancellations and the claimed INTEGRAL homotopy wedge. Fifty-two size-six faces are missing, excluding the high-skeleton shortcut. Pure dimension six with H5 nonzero is nonshellable. This is a complete finite result, not an infinite extrapolation.
residual_risks: Self-contained exact finite reconstruction does not itself certify the historic original tree identity; locked Git blobs and source tree SHA guard supplied.

evidence: Bayer et al., Topology of Cut Complexes of Graphs, arXiv:2304.13675, Thm 6.1: its high-skeleton hypothesis fails because 52 six-vertex faces are absent; Bayer et al. Topology of Cut Complexes II arXiv:2407.08158 treats disjoint unions, squared paths, grids, not L(Q3). Published cuboctahedral 3-cut concerns k=3 not k=5.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Bayer et al high-skeleton theorem is inapplicable because 52 size-six faces are missing; the other same-graph published complexes have different facets.
